dimensions.note: A private key reaches a short-lived ssh-agent over stdin; a password goes through a temporary askpass helper and an environment variable; neither appears in ssh argv (tested). Secret fields are sensitive-marked. 2026.10.17.2: upload no longer sends the expected content SHA-256 to the remote; the remote prints the destination's own SHA-256 and mode after the rename and the comparison runs locally, so no content-derived digest appears on any spawned argv or in remote script text for upload (probe and write), exec or execPipeline (new unit test asserts no 64-hex string on any argv). exec returns only exit code and SHA-256 of stdout/stderr; raw output is stored only in the sensitive execution resource when return_output is set. Residual MEDIUM (terra, carried from 2026.10.17.1; raised as HIGH in the delta round and refuted as a regression): the SHA-256 of low-entropy output or content returned in results and resources could be guessed; hashes in place of raw content is the design the run rulings require. Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: the CLI prints literal sensitive arguments, so README examples use vault references only and never --json.
Each method logs once with structured placeholders (host, port, exit code, changed, key count); no secret, argv or output in log fields.

A remote non-zero exit is returned as data; every OpenSSH exit 255 maps to a typed SshError (host key, auth, unreachable, transport), live-verified. Typed SshConfigError for bad policy, pins that match nothing for the host, and a supplied pin that disagrees with the recorded pin. Output over max_output_bytes kills the child with a typed error. upload now fails with a typed 'did not converge' SshError when the post-rename hash or mode read back differs. Residual MEDIUM (terra, new in 2026.10.17.2): the post-rename check reads the first stdout token, so a target whose forced-command wrapper prints to stdout fails upload after the rename; it fails closed, never a false success. Residual MEDIUM (carried): a Linux target without sha256sum/shasum fails only after the rename.

65 unit tests with an injected runner, clock and sleep (no process or socket), including a new test that no content-derived 64-hex string reaches any spawned argv or script text, and upload fakes that return the post-rename hash and mode. Live end-to-end matrix: 23/23 on 2026.10.17.1 (on stable). For 2026.10.17.2 the 17 non-upload cells carry over (code path byte-identical); the six upload cells (3, 3b, 10, X2, X3, X4) are pending re-run on 2026.10.17.2, which beta allows; they must pass before promotion to stable.

upload probes the destination SHA-256 and mode and skips the write (no new resource version) when both match (probe unchanged from 2026.10.17.1, live-verified there); a mode-only change goes through the temp-file mv -T path, and the post-rename read-back now checks both hash and mode locally. insecure_tofu pins are committed only after the transport succeeds. Residual MEDIUM (carried, downgraded under the run rulings): two simultaneous first-use calls can race on the pin write.

Built on the OpenSSH client, ssh-agent/ssh-add and ssh-keyscan with -F /dev/null and IdentityFile=none, so the operator's ssh config is never consulted. upload requires GNU mv -T and fails closed on non-Linux targets.

Temporary known_hosts, askpass helper and ssh-agent are removed or killed in finally (tested). Remote output is streamed with a cap (default 10 MiB, max 100 MiB). Residual MEDIUM (astra, terra): ssh-keyscan output is not capped; scan output is small and the cap is a follow-up.

Manifest: @randybias/ssh-host 2026.10.17.2 (model version literals match), two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt. exec and upload descriptions start DESTRUCTIVE. Fixtures use RFC 5737 addresses and low-entropy synthetic host keys; leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Residual LOW (astra, carried): the exec and upload descriptions describe return_output and mode-only changes inaccurately. LOW (astra, delta): a redundant exact-hash assertion in the new test.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; host, user, port, remote path and mode carry grammars; argv rejects NUL and every word is POSIX-quoted, live-verified against injection. host_keys and argv are bounded. host_key_policy is required with no default; strict requires pins. Residual MEDIUM (astra): argv words have no allowlist grammar beyond NUL; quoting is the defence for a generic exec primitive.
execution, upload and connection resources: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 10.

Transport primitive with three action methods: exec, upload and wait_connection. It owns no remote resource lifecycle, so there is no create/delete; consumers (server-host, wireguard-mesh, k0s-cluster) own that.

Policy, pins and paths are validated before any spawn; strict without pins, pins for another host and a pin that disagrees with the record are refused before connecting. upload refuses a directory, symlink, trailing slash or dot component before writing and re-checks around the rename (mv -T, symlink and directory refusal unchanged in 2026.10.17.2).

Length-prefixed components avoid collisions: the TOFU pin is connection-h<len>-<host>-p<port> (host+port, known_hosts semantics, so a second user is verified against the same pin); exec and upload evidence add u<len>-<user>.
Methods read only this model's own connection resource for the pin; every target arrives as method arguments, so one generic definition serves any host.

2026.10.17.2 is a point release of 2026.10.17.1 with no schema, argument, resource or instance-name change; data written by 2026.10.17.1 is read unchanged. The vendored _lib/ssh.ts blob is now fe0139f08c42e3fdae0061b9688fb5c534174957; vendors resync to it.
